title: Fractions
goal: Add, subtract, compare, multiply and simplify fractions.

lesson_media.alt: Three equal-length fraction bars show one of two, two of four and four of eight equal parts shaded, each covering exactly half of its bar.
lesson_media.caption: One half, two quarters and four eighths are equivalent fractions: the partitions change, but the shaded amount stays the same.

lesson_media.title: Build equivalent fractions
lesson_media.instructions: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the same factor. Watch the partitions change while the fraction's value stays the same.

quiz.explain: Use a common denominator of 12: 2/3 = 8/12 and 1/4 = 3/12, so the sum is 11/12.

quiz.prompt: Sam says 3/8 must be bigger than 2/5, because 8 is bigger than 5. Which reply is correct?
choices: Sam is right: a bigger bottom number means more
Sam is wrong: the two fractions turn out equal
Sam is right: 3 pieces beats 2 pieces
quiz.explain: Both fractions refer to the same-sized whole. Over a common denominator of 40, 3/8 becomes 15/40 and 2/5 becomes 16/40, so 2/5 is larger. The denominator says how many equal parts make the whole; by itself it does not tell you which fraction is larger.
One quarter of 20 is 5, so three quarters is 3 x 5 = 15.

quiz.prompt: Simplify 18/24 to its lowest terms. What is the denominator of the simplified fraction?
quiz.explain: Dividing top and bottom by 6 gives 3/4, so the denominator is 4.

quiz.prompt: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. You eat 3 slices and a friend eats 2. What fraction of the pizza is left?
quiz.explain: Five slices are gone, so 3 of the 8 slices remain: 3/8.

quiz.prompt: A recipe needs 1/2 a cup of sugar and you have 3/4 of a cup. How much is left once you measure out what the recipe needs?
quiz.explain: 3/4 - 1/2 = 3/4 - 2/4 = 1/4 of a cup. Subtracting tops and bottoms separately would wrongly give 2/2.
Divide 45 into 5 equal parts of 9, then take 2 of them: 2 x 9 = 18.

quiz.prompt: Simplify 30/45 to its lowest terms. What is the numerator of the simplified fraction?
quiz.explain: Both numbers divide by 15, giving 2/3, so the numerator is 2.

quiz.prompt: Ali multiplies 1/2 by 1/3 and writes 2/6, saying you add the tops and multiply the bottoms. What went wrong?
quiz.answer: He added the numerators instead of multiplying them
choices: He added the numerators instead of multiplying them
He needed a common denominator first
He should have turned the second fraction upside down
He forgot to simplify at the end
quiz.explain: To multiply fractions you multiply top by top and bottom by bottom: 1/2 x 1/3 = 1/6. Common denominators are needed when adding or subtracting fractions with unlike denominators, not when multiplying.

quiz.prompt: Which of these is a sound first step for adding 1/6 and 1/4?
choices: Add the tops and add the bottoms
Rewrite both of them with tenths
Multiply the two bottoms and keep the tops as they are
quiz.explain: The smallest number both 6 and 4 divide into is 12, so 1/6 = 2/12 and 1/4 = 3/12, giving 5/12.
